segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Every place a song goes quiet, they've been there first. I thought if I followed long enough, I'd find the verse they were hiding.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Can't, or won't?

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: I'm coming with you to the Keep. If anyone hears that verse sung at last, it's going to be me.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Pay it back, children, or pay what you've known.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Twenty years. And it was sitting in a tower all along, waiting for someone to ask.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Whatever you choose up there, every square in the Vale will know what the choice was. I'll make sure of it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Ah, an audience! Stand there and look grave, and I'll sing you something the Wardens wrote before your grandmothers were born.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Look at you. Still holding a lute like it owes you money.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: I left because the songs were moving, and a songkeeper has to move with them. I should have said goodbye. We're terrible at endings. We always think there's another verse.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Stay close this time. If the songs are right, the Vale is about to need someone who can tell the whole of it.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Seven went over the Greywall high, and seven came home with a fire in the sky. The Wardens kept it and the Wardens sang, and the whole Vale warmed where the hearth-bells rang.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: That's the Wardens' Song of the Seven. Seven went, seven came home, a gift and a hearth and everyone happy.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: There's a last verse, too. Nobody has sung it in two hundred years. When a song loses its last verse on purpose, it's usually because the last verse was true.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Songs gather where things are about to happen. A starving town, a goblin on a bridge, an ember going cold under the river. This is the best stage in the Vale.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: And someone I've been following came this way. Never mind who. That's a song for later, somewhere colder.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Anything else? I take requests. I don't take criticism.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Go on, then. Do something worth a verse.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: The bridge ballad's a sad one now. They always are, when you write them honestly.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: A truce at the ford! I'll need a whole new verse. Possibly three.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Bree goes back to the bar, a tune drifts over from the corner table, where a travelling minstrel has been listening the whole time.
